title: Meet on the Rooftop
covers: how to find the least common multiple of two numbers by skip counting their multiples and finding the first match
cert: finding the least common multiple by listing multiples and finding the first match

intro.caption: Lesson 6-12 — least common multiple. Chip chased a moth up the tower antenna and now he can't get down. The rescue ladder takes two agents, but both are stuck on patrol drills. Three gates and a boss lock stand between the cadets and the rescue.

balloons.t: The ladder needs two agents at the hatch at the same time. Ozzie and I are both on patrol drills.
No rush. I love it up here. The wind. The cold. The very large bird.
Farah's loop has 4 stops. Ozzie's has 6. Each round, they move one stop.
Both back at the hatch? Easy. 4 times 6 is 24. Round 24. That's classified.
24 works. But is it the FIRST time? Chip can't wait extra rounds. Let's list.

pages.caption: Teo multiplied the two numbers. That always gives a common multiple, but maybe not the least one.

balloons.t: I'm at the hatch every 4th round. Skip count by 4!
Two lists. Look for the first number in BOTH.
Wait. The ladder is short. Ivy and I need to bring the second half.
Three locks. My code: just multiply. It's always the product, rookies.
Rescued in the least number of rounds. I'll allow it.

win.caption: The least common multiple is the FIRST number in both lists of multiples. The product of the two numbers is always a common multiple, but it is often not the least one.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Skip Count
gates.prompt: Farah is at the hatch every 4th round. Ozzie is there every 6th round. List their rounds.
hints: Conceptual: a multiple of 4 is what you get when you multiply 4 by 1, 2, 3, and so on.
Procedural: skip count out loud. Start at the number and keep adding it again.

steps: Practice loop: an agent with a 3-stop loop is at the hatch every 3rd round.
Each of those is a multiple of 3: 3 × 1, 3 × 2, 3 × 3, 3 × 4, 3 × 5.
worked.q: List the first four multiples of 5.

items.q: Which rounds put Farah (every 4th round) at the hatch? Pick all that apply.

options.fb: 14 is not a multiple of 4. Skip counting goes 12, then 16.
6 is Ozzie's first round. 4 does not go into 6 evenly.

items.fbMiss: You missed a multiple of 4. Skip count: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20.
items.fbExtra: One of your picks is not a multiple of 4. Does 4 go into it evenly?

items.label: Ozzie's 5th time at the hatch is round

fb.msg: That's 6 + 5. The 5th multiple is 6 × 5. Skip count by 6 five times.
24 is his 4th time: 6, 12, 18, 24. One more skip.

gates.pass: Farah: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. Ozzie: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. Two lists on the screen.

gates.title: Gate 2 · The First Match
gates.prompt: Farah's rounds are multiples of 4. Ozzie's are multiples of 6. When are they first at the hatch together?
hints: Conceptual: a common multiple is in BOTH lists. The least common multiple is the first one you meet.
Procedural: skip count the bigger number, 6, 12, 18… and stop at the first one that 4 also goes into.

steps: Practice: the LCM of 6 and 8. Skip count the bigger number: 8, 16, 24.
Check each against 6: 8 no, 16 no, 24 yes (6 × 4 = 24).
So the LCM is 24. The product 6 × 8 = 48 is a common multiple, but 24 comes first.
worked.q: What is the LCM of 6 and 10?

items.label: First round they are BOTH at the hatch:

fb.msg: 24 is 4 × 6. It is in both lists, but it is not the FIRST match. Check 12.
2 goes INTO both numbers. That's a common factor. You want a number both go into.
That's 4 + 6. Is 10 in Ozzie's list? 6, 12, 18… no.

items.fbDefault: Write both lists and find the first number in both.

items.q: Which list shows common multiples of 4 and 6?

options.fb: 4 and 8 are not multiples of 6, and 6 is not a multiple of 4.
1 and 2 are common FACTORS. They go into 4 and 6, not the other way.
10 is 4 + 6, and 4 does not go into 10, 30… These are multiples of 10.

gates.pass: Round 12. Both agents at the hatch — twelve rounds sooner than Teo's 24.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Second Ladder
gates.prompt: Ivy runs an 8-stop loop. Teo runs a 10-stop loop. Both start at the hatch. Plan the meeting.
hints: Conceptual: you want the least number that both 8 and 10 go into evenly.
Procedural: skip count by 10 (the bigger number). Stop at the first one that 8 also goes into.

steps: Practice: loops of 6 and 9 stops. Skip count by 9: 9, 18.
They meet at round 18, not at 6 × 9 = 54.
worked.q: Loops of 8 and 12 stops. First meeting round?

items.label: Ivy and Teo first meet at round

fb.msg: 80 is 8 × 10, the product. It works, but 40 is in both lists first.
2 is a common factor of 8 and 10. You want a common MULTIPLE.
That's 8 + 10. Neither 8 nor 10 goes into 18 evenly.
20 is a multiple of 10, but 8 does not go into 20 evenly.

items.fbDefault: Skip count by 10: 10, 20, 30, 40… Which one does 8 go into?

items.q: Teo says: "The LCM of 8 and 10 is 80, because you always multiply." Is he right?

options.t: Yes. Multiplying always gives the LCM.
options.fb: Multiplying gives A common multiple. It is not always the least. 40 comes first here.

options.t: No. 80 is a common multiple, but 40 comes first.

options.fb: 2 is the greatest common factor. The LCM is a number both go INTO.

gates.pass: Round 40: the second ladder half arrives. Teo says the number 80 was "a decoy." Nobody believes him.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Vale's Hatch
gates.prompt: Vale's hatch has three locks. Each one is an LCM. Don't trust "just multiply."
hints: Conceptual: the LCM is the first number in both lists of multiples. The product is in both lists, but it may not be first.
Procedural: skip count the bigger number and test each one against the smaller number.

steps: Practice lock: the LCM of 8 and 12.
LCM = 24. The product 8 × 12 = 96 is far too big.
worked.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 10?

items.label: Lock 1 · LCM of 9 and 12:

fb.msg: 108 is 9 × 12. Vale's trick! Skip count by 12 and stop at the first one 9 goes into.
3 is the greatest common factor. The LCM is a number both go into.
That's 9 + 12. 9 does not go into 21 evenly.

items.fbDefault: Skip count by 12: 12, 24, 36… Which is the first one 9 goes into?

items.label: Lock 2 · Glow sticks come in packs of 6, batteries in packs of 8. Fewest glow sticks you can have when the number of glow sticks equals the number of batteries (whole packs only):
items.aria: fewest glow sticks, least common multiple of 6 and 8

fb.msg: 48 is 6 × 8. That works, but 24 is in both lists first.
That's 6 + 8. Neither pack size goes into 14 evenly.
2 is a common factor. You want a common multiple.

items.fbDefault: Skip count by 8: 8, 16, 24… Which is the first one 6 goes into?

items.q: Lock 3 · What is the LCM of 5 and 7?

options.fb: 70 is a common multiple, but 35 is in both lists first.
1 is the only common factor. The LCM is a multiple, so it is at least 7.

gates.pass: CLICK, CLICK, CLICK. 36, 24, 35. This time the product WAS the LCM (5 and 7 share no factor but 1). Vale's rule only works sometimes.

journal.heading: Lesson 6-12 — what the rooftop rescue taught us
rows: Skip count to list multiples. Farah's 4-stop loop: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. Ozzie's 6-stop loop: 6, 12, 18, 24.
A common multiple is in both lists. 12, 24 and 36 are all common multiples of 4 and 6.
The LCM is the FIRST match. The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12, so the agents meet at round 12.
4 × 6 = 24 is a common multiple, but not the least. The product is the LCM only when the numbers share no factor but 1, like 5 and 7.
journal.quote: "Multiplying gets you there eventually. Listing gets me down sooner." — Chip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 6-12 (Least Common Multiple) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: listing multiples by skip counting, finding common multiples, choosing the first match as the LCM, and why the product of two numbers is not always the LCM.
standards: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers ≤ 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers ≤ 12
